### Step 1: Examine the Differences

$$
\begin{align*}
a(1) - a(0) &= 32 - 1 = 31 \\

a(3) - a(2) &= 272 - 122 = 150 \\
a(4) - a(3) &= 482 - 272 = 210 \\
a(5) - a(4) &= 752 - 482 = 270 \\
\end{align*}
$$

$$

150 - 90 &= 60 \\

$$

### Step 2: Assume a Quadratic Form

Let’s assume for $ n \geq 2 $, the sequence follows the form:

$$
a(n) = An^2 + Bn + C
$$

We use the values at $ n = 2, 3, 4 $ to solve for $ A, B, C $:

$$
\begin{align*}
a(2) &= 122 = 4A + 2B + C \\
a(3) &= 272 = 9A + 3B + C \\
a(4) &= 482 = 16A + 4B + C \\
\end{align*}
$$

Subtracting the first from the second:

$$
(9A + 3B + C) - (4A + 2B + C) = 5A + B = 150 \quad \text{(1)}
$$

Subtracting the second from the third:

$$
(16A + 4B + C) - (9A + 3B + C) = 7A + B = 210 \quad \text{(2)}
$$

Subtracting (1) from (2):

$$
(7A + B) - (5A + B) = 2A = 60 \Rightarrow A = 30
$$

$$
4(30) + 2(0) + C = 122 \Rightarrow 120 + C = 122 \Rightarrow C = 2
$$

Thus, for $ n \geq 2 $, the sequence is:

$$
a(n) = 30n^2 + 2
$$

We verify this formula for $ n = 2, 3, 4, 5 $:

$$
\begin{align*}
a(2) &= 30(4) + 2 = 122 \\
a(3) &= 30(9) + 2 = 272 \\
a(4) &= 30(16) + 2 = 482 \\
a(5) &= 30(25) + 2 = 752 \\
\end{align*}
$$
